exams.name: Board examination
exams.notes: The board determines the subjects; examination may be waived under license-by-credentials provision (AS 08.64.250).
exams.quote: An applicant shall take examinations in subjects the board considers necessary, unless excused under provisions of AS 08.64.250.

interval_years.quote: The fee for a permit issued under this section is one-fourth of the fee for a biennial license

required.quote: The board shall promote a high degree of competence in the practice of medicine, osteopathy, and podiatry by requiring every licensee of medicine, osteopathy, and podiatry in the state to fulfill continuing education requirements.

period_years.quote: not less than two hours of education in pain management and opioid use and addiction in the two years preceding an application for renewal of a license

value: pain management and opioid use and addiction (minimum 2 hours per 2-year renewal cycle)
topical_requirements.quote: Continuing education requirements must include not less than two hours of education in pain management and opioid use and addiction in the two years preceding an application for renewal of a license

available.quote: The board may waive the examination requirement and license by credentials if the physician, osteopath, or podiatry applicant meets the requirements of AS 08.64.200, 08.64.205, or 08.64.209, submits proof of continued competence as required by regulation, pays the required fee, and has an active license from a board of medical examiners established under the laws of a state or territory of the United States or a province or territory of Canada issued after thorough examination

requirements.value: Active license from another U.S. state/territory or Canadian province/territory issued after thorough examination; must also meet all other qualifications (education, malpractice disclosure, pain management education) and submit proof of continued competence.
requirements.quote: The board may waive the examination requirement and license by credentials if the physician, osteopath, or podiatry applicant meets the requirements of AS 08.64.200, 08.64.205, or 08.64.209, submits proof of continued competence as required by regulation, pays the required fee, and has an active license from a board of medical examiners established under the laws of a state or territory of the United States or a province or territory of Canada issued after thorough examination

disciplinary_grounds.quote: intentionally or negligently permitted the performance of patient care by persons under the licensee's supervision that does not conform to minimum professional standards even if the patient was not injured

disciplinary_grounds.quote: unfitness because of physical or mental disability

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribed or dispensed an opioid in excess of the maximum dosage authorized under AS 08.64.363
disciplinary_grounds.quote: prescribed or dispensed an opioid in excess of the maximum dosage authorized under AS 08.64.363

definition_quote.value: for a fee, donation or other consideration, to diagnose, treat, operate on, prescribe for, or administer to, any human ailment, blemish, deformity, disease, disfigurement, disorder, injury, or other mental or physical condition; or to attempt to perform or represent that a person is authorized to perform any of the acts set out in this subparagraph
definition_quote.quote: for a fee, donation or other consideration, to diagnose, treat, operate on, prescribe for, or administer to, any human ailment, blemish, deformity, disease, disfigurement, disorder, injury, or other mental or physical condition; or to attempt to perform or represent that a person is authorized to perform any of the acts set out in this subparagraph

methods_authorized.quote: to diagnose, treat, operate on, prescribe for, or administer to, any human ailment, blemish, deformity, disease, disfigurement, disorder, injury, or other mental or physical condition

drug_authority.value: Licensees may prescribe, dispense, and administer drugs including controlled substances, subject to opioid prescribing limits and telehealth rules.
drug_authority.quote: has procured, sold, prescribed, or dispensed drugs in violation of a law regardless of whether there has been a criminal action or harm to the patient

license_status_types.quote: A licensee who does not practice in the state may hold an inactive license. A person who practices in the state, however infrequently, shall hold an active license.

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates must meet requirements of AS 08.64.200(a)(3)-(5) and 08.64.255, complete three years of postgraduate training (or alternative board-approved proof of competency), and pass board-specified examinations.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: Applicants who are graduates of medical colleges not accredited by the Association of American Medical Colleges and the Council on Medical Education of the American Medical Association shall meet the requirements of AS 08.64.200(a)(3) - (5) and 08.64.255; have successfully completed three years of postgraduate training

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: two years if the applicant graduated from medical school on or after January 1, 1995, as evidenced by a certificate of completion of the first year of postgraduate training from the facility where the applicant completed the first year of internship or residency and a certificate of successful completion of one additional year of postgraduate training at a recognized hospital

pain_management_education_required.quote: receive education in pain management and opioid use and addiction, unless the applicant has demonstrated to the satisfaction of the board that the applicant does not currently hold a valid federal Drug Enforcement Administration registration number

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: Initial opioid prescription may not exceed a seven-day supply for adult outpatients; prescriptions for minors may not exceed a seven-day supply. Exceptions exist for chronic pain, cancer, palliative care, logistical/travel barriers, and substance abuse treatment.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: A licensee may not issue an initial prescription for an opioid that exceeds a seven-day supply to an adult patient for outpatient use; a prescription for an opioid that exceeds a seven-day supply to a minor

controlled_substance_database_registrati.quote: require that a licensee who has a federal Drug Enforcement Administration registration number register with the controlled substance prescription database under AS 17.30.200(n)

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: Board may not impose disciplinary sanctions for prescribing non-controlled substances via telehealth if follow-up care is available and records are shared with primary care provider with patient consent; controlled substances may also be prescribed if those conditions plus opioid limits are met. Prescribing in response to internet questionnaire or email without prior physician-patient relationship is prohibited.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: The board may not impose disciplinary sanctions on a physician or physician assistant for rendering a diagnosis, providing treatment, or prescribing, dispensing, or administering a prescription drug that is not a controlled substance to a person without conducting a physical examination if the physician, physician assistant, or another licensed health care provider in the medical practice is available to provide follow-up care

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: a physician assistant may examine, diagnose, or treat persons under the supervision, control, and responsibility of either a physician licensed under this chapter or a physician exempted from licensing under AS 08.64.370

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: Physician assistants may prescribe drugs (including controlled substances via telehealth) subject to the same conditions as physicians under AS 08.64.364; duties related to pain management and opioid use and addiction may not be delegated.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: The board may not impose disciplinary sanctions on a physician or physician assistant for rendering a diagnosis, providing treatment, or prescribing, dispensing, or administering a prescription drug that is not a controlled substance to a person without conducting a physical examination

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: A person licensed under this chapter shall report in writing to the board concerning the outcome of each medical malpractice claim or civil action in which damages have been or are to be paid by or on behalf of the licensee to the claimant or plaintiff, whether by judgment or under a settlement.

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: A hospital that revokes, suspends, conditions, restricts, or refuses to grant hospital privileges to, or imposes a consultation requirement on, a person licensed to practice medicine or osteopathy in the state shall report to the board the name and address of the person and the reasons for the action within seven working days after the action is taken.

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: under regulations adopted by the board, contract with private professional organizations to establish an impaired medical professionals program to identify, confront, evaluate, and treat persons licensed under this chapter who abuse alcohol, other drugs, or other substances or are mentally ill or cognitively impaired

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: For the purposes of an investigation under this chapter, the board may order a person to whom it has issued a license or permit to submit to a medical or psychiatric examination by a physician or other practitioner of the healing arts appointed by the board.

locum_tenens_permit_available.quote: A member of the board, its executive secretary, or a person designated by the board to issue temporary permits may grant a temporary permit to a physician or osteopath for the purpose of substituting for another physician or osteopath licensed in this state

investigational_drug_protection.quote: A physician may not be subject to disciplinary action by the board for prescribing, dispensing, or administering an investigational drug, biological product, or device, or providing related treatment, to a patient for the purpose of sustaining the patient's life if the patient has a terminal illness
